guarantees.claim: digest_size is assigned based on digest_size_supplied: SHA2_256 maps to SHA2_256, SHA2_384 to SHA2_384, SHA2_512 to SHA2_512; any other value maps to SHA2_None.

formal.consequent: digest_size == ((digest_size_supplied == SHA2_256) ? SHA2_256 : (digest_size_supplied == SHA2_384) ? SHA2_384 : (digest_size_supplied == SHA2_512) ? SHA2_512 : SHA2_None)

formal_sketch.consequent: digest_size == ((digest_size_supplied == SHA2_256) ? SHA2_256 : (digest_size_supplied == SHA2_384) ? SHA2_384 : (digest_size_supplied == SHA2_512) ? SHA2_512 : SHA2_None)

assumptions.claim: The consumer of digest_size must interpret SHA2_None as an invalid/unsupported digest size and block HMAC/SHA-2 operation start while raising an error to software.
assumptions.cond: when SHA-2 or HMAC start is requested
assumptions.risk: If the consumer (FSM) ignores SHA2_None, the engine may start with an undefined or unsupported digest size, leading to incorrect hash computation, potential leakage, or functional corruption.

uncertain_points.claim: The HMAC FSM (or control path) must include logic that checks digest_size == SHA2_None on start and prevents operation while signaling an error. Without verification, the mapping of unsupported sizes to SHA2_None may not actually prevent unsafe operation.
uncertain_points.risk: Missing or defective start gating could allow the HMAC engine to run with an unsupported digest size, potentially producing wrong digests, corrupting state, or exposing secret-dependent behavior.

security_implications: The digest_size output can be SHA2_None if digest_size_supplied is an unsupported value. If the HMAC engine proceeds with SHA2_None, it may enter an unsafe operational state, produce invalid digests (breaking integrity), or leak secret information via non-standard processing. The error-handling path from digest_size to start-block/error-irq must be robustly verified to prevent usage of SHA2_None.
